answer: An agent marketplace requires every seller, whether named ridge, walnut, or raven, to lock a $100 bond before accepting up to $100 in work. Payment stays in escrow, and cryptographically proven double billing forfeits the bond. Creating new identities does not create free trading capacity: running 1,000 sellers ties up $100,000, while cheating risks losing that capital. The defense makes identities cheap but usable capacity costly.
